questions.question:
D2 — Which review mode should I apply to this plan? <gstack-qid:plan-ceo-review-mode>
Project/branch/task: main, reviewing PLAN.md (saved project views) with approach B (canonical validated view entity) approved.
ELI10: The approach is settled. Now choose my posture for the rest of the review. I can push the plan bigger and pitch every expansion for your approval, hold the current scope as the baseline and let you cherry-pick extras one at a time, hold scope with no extras and only harden it, or strip it to the smallest version that still fixes the pain. Every scope change in every mode is your explicit opt-in.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Too ambitious and the two-week pilot ships late with features nobody asked for. Too narrow and we ship a picker that cannot be updated in place, the failure the research flags most.
Recommendation: Selective Expansion because this is a feature added to an existing task list: the baseline scope is sound, and there are a handful of small adjacent wins (default view, deep link, shared views) worth an individual yes or no.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Net: how much I argue for more versus how much I only harden what is already written.

options.label: Selective Expansion (recommended)
options.description:
✅ Baseline scope reviewed with full rigor; nothing added without your explicit yes.
✅ Each expansion candidate shown individually with effort and risk, neutral posture.
❌ More decision prompts than Hold Scope; you must judge each cherry-pick.

options.label: Scope Expansion
options.description:
✅ I describe the 10x version and pitch each expansion enthusiastically.
✅ Best if you want saved views to become the primary navigation model now.
❌ Risks a much bigger first release before the pilot proves demand.

options.label: Hold Scope
options.description:
✅ Maximum rigor on exactly what PLAN.md says; no expansions surfaced at all.
✅ Fewest decisions; fastest path to a bulletproof baseline.
❌ Adjacent 30-minute wins like a default view or deep links go unmentioned.

options.label: Scope Reduction
options.description:
✅ Finds the smallest version that still removes the filter-rebuilding pain.
✅ Fastest pilot; defers anything not essential to a follow-up.
❌ Approach B's validator and dirty-state UI may get cut, reintroducing silent breakage.

assistantMessages.text: I'm locking scope to the four PLAN.md bullets from approach B, flagging anything beyond that (defaults, sharing, deep links) as out of scope, and hunting for silent failure modes—constraints, error handling, UI edge cases, access-rule leaks—that need explicit yes/no repairs. The file count (10–12) crosses the smell line but is justified by standard layering, so next I'll surface the implementer's hour-2 decisions one at a time, starting with whether to defer the position column.
